newsitem.title: USA: Shorewood to sell transportation business.
newsitem.headline: Shorewood to sell transportation business.

text.p: Shorewood Packaging Corp said Wednesday it will sell its transportation business because it no longer fits within the company's core operations and will seek outside services for its future delivery needs.

Marc Shore, chairman of the company, said the business, which is operated through its Shorewood Transport Inc unit, had been lately losing money. The unit provides freight delivery services to Shorewood Packaging and to other non-related customers. "The purpose for its existence years ago can be fulfilled today by outside freight companies without compromising the service to our customers," he said.
Outsourcing the function will not only eliminate the recent operating losses, he said, but will significantly reduce the the company's future freight and delivery expenses.
He said that the unit's revenues generated from non-related customers for the first nine months of fiscal 1997 were $4.925 million, which resulted in an operating loss of $599,000.
The company said it estimates a loss arising from the disposal at approximately $800,000 or $494,000 net of taxes, translating to $.03 per share, which will be recorded in the fourth quarter.
Operating results for all prior periods will be restated to reflect the operations of the unit as discontinued operations, it said.
In so doing, it said operating results from continuing operations for fiscal 1997 will be improved.
